title: Quantum Applications
learning_goal: Describe examples of quantum uncertainty and modern applications including quantum computing and cybersecurity.

stages.title: 1. Quantum uncertainty
stages.content: The uncertainty principle places a fundamental limit on how precisely certain pairs of physical quantities, such as position and momentum, can be known at the same time.

stages.title: 2. Quantum computing
stages.content: Quantum computers use quantum states called qubits. Superposition and entanglement can allow some computations to be structured very differently from classical computing.

stages.title: 3. Quantum and cybersecurity
stages.content: Quantum technologies can affect cybersecurity in two directions: some quantum algorithms threaten certain current encryption methods, while quantum key distribution can reveal attempts to intercept a key.

stages.title: 4. Other applications
stages.content: Quantum physics also underlies technologies such as lasers, semiconductors, LEDs, medical imaging components, atomic clocks, and precision sensors.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Why can quantum key distribution reveal eavesdropping attempts?
stages.hint: Think about what measurement does to a quantum state.
stages.alternate_explanation: Measuring an unknown quantum state can disturb it, creating detectable changes in the communication.
stages.answer: Because interception and measurement can disturb the quantum states and reveal that the key exchange was observed.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, explain uncertainty in plain language, identify the role of qubits in quantum computing, describe a cybersecurity application, and connect quantum physics to modern technologies.
